name: Alaska
agency: Alaska Department of Administration, Division of Motor Vehicles

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours, at least 10 in challenging conditions (night or bad weather)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months, with no traffic or alcohol/drug violations
teen.nightLimit: Provisional license: no driving 1:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. unless with a licensed driver 21+ or for work
teen.passengerLimit: Provisional license: no passengers under 21 except siblings, unless a licensed driver 21+ is in the car
teen.phone: All drivers: no reading or typing texts while the vehicle is moving (AS 28.35.161); no handheld-call ban found

bac.under21: any detectable amount (zero tolerance; one source says 0.02)

notes: Permit supervisor must be a licensed driver 21+ with at least one year of experience in that kind of vehicle, in the front passenger seat.
Provisional restrictions end at 18 or after 6 months on the provisional license without violations.
Default maximum speeds (13 AAC 02.275): 15 mph alley, 20 mph business district, 25 mph residential district, 55 mph other roads unless posted. Some rural interstates are posted 65 mph.
Headlights required from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise and whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen at 1,000 feet; also on roads posted for headlights.
Slow driver on a two-lane road outside urban areas with 5 or more vehicles lined up behind must pull into the nearest turnout (13 AAC 02.050).
School bus with flashing red lights: stop at least 30 feet away, from either direction (AS 28.35.145). Divided-highway exception wording not confirmed.
Move over: stationary emergency vehicles with flashing lights (AS 28.35.185): change lanes if safe, otherwise slow down.
Right turn on red allowed after a full stop unless a sign forbids it.
Implied consent: refusing a breath test is a separate crime.
Knowledge test may be taken online (KnowToDrive) per third-party sources; not confirmed.
Pending bills (HB 213 / SB 249) proposed 50 hours and longer provisional period; not confirmed as enacted.
Official dmv.alaska.gov / doa.alaska.gov could not be fetched from this environment; facts come from search snippets of those pages.
Owner-supplied summary of the Alaska Driver Manual (2026-10-09), not yet checked against the text: manual updated October 2025; instruction permit from age 14; minimum following distance 4 seconds.

Same summary: the online knowledge test (KnowToDrive) offers a choice of language and read-aloud; a person who understands English but has trouble reading may bring someone to read the questions aloud, if they answer alone. Worth mentioning to Alaska learners.
